clue.text: Tournament where merry men gathered

parts.note: a contest in which every player meets every other, pictured as the outlaw band of Sherwood clustering about their leader

explanation.surface: Sherwood's outlaws assemble for a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin Hood's band were his 'merry men'; gathered about him they are literally grouped around their leader, which is also the name of an all-play-all competition.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-play-all competition, where each entrant faces every other entrant, is the standard sense of the phrase.

clue.text: In public, he, Henry, and I will appear past our prime

parts.note: overt means public, done openly
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance
I'll is the contraction of I will

explanation.surface: Two people say they will appear openly though they are getting old.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'past our prime' needs a phrase meaning elderly; 'In' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Being past one's best years, too old for something, is the idiom's meaning.

clue.text: There's nothing to equal it — it can be made no plainer

indicators.note: can be made says the letters may be remade into another word

explanation.surface: An unrivalled thing could not be any simpler.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing without equal, unmatched and unrivalled.

clue.text: In Henley, for instance, soldier is given gun by army

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, stands for a soldier
gat is slang for a gun
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: At Henley a soldier is handed a weapon by the army.
explanation.walkthrough: Henley-on-Thames hosts a famous annual rowing event; 'In' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Henley's Royal event is the best-known boat race meeting, a regatta.

clue.text: Having negotiated flight downwards, seek lower prices here?

definitions.text: Having negotiated flight downwards, seek lower prices here?

parts.words: Having negotiated flight downwards, seek lower prices here?
parts.note: a shop's cheapest floor, reached by going down the stairs, where reduced goods are haggled over

explanation.surface: After descending the stairs, a shopper hunts for reduced goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Negotiated' hints at haggling over a deal, and the 'flight downwards' is a staircase to the floor below street level.
explanation.definitionFit: A department store's cheap lower-ground floor selling reduced-price goods.

clue.text: Screw unfinished drawing up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from bottom to top
unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: drawing, as in pulling along, means dragging

explanation.surface: A screw left half-turned while sketching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' drops the last letter of DRAGGING to give DRAGGIN, and 'up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A screw is British slang for a miser, a stingy person.

clue.text: Wardrobe to 'boast about

indicators.note: about signals turning round, so the word for boasting is read from its end to its start

parts.note: to boast is to brag

explanation.surface: Someone's clothes are a reason to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: A wardrobe in the sense of a person's whole stock of clothes is their attire or dress.

clue.text: Easy pace of relaxing walk, with no runs involved

indicators.note: with no tells us a letter is removed from the word for a stroll

parts.note: a ramble is a leisurely walk
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A gentle stroll where nobody runs.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely walking gait, an unhurried stroll.

clue.text: Wood, a piece of log cut up

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the letters are read from the bottom

parts.note: a slab is a thick flat piece cut from a log

explanation.surface: Timber made by sawing a log.
explanation.definitionFit: A very light timber from a tropical American tree, used for models and rafts.

clue.text: Youngster facing a seven year stretch

definitions.text: Youngster facing a seven year stretch

parts.words: Youngster facing a seven year stretch
parts.note: the stretch is not a prison term but the seven years from thirteen to nineteen, which a twelve-year-old is about to enter

explanation.surface: A young offender is about to be sent down for seven years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretch' suggests a jail sentence; the seven years are the ages ending in -teen.
explanation.definitionFit: An adolescent is a young person aged thirteen to nineteen, the seven years whose numbers end in -teen.

clue.text: Frolic lands doctor in prison

indicators.note: in tells us the doctor's letters sit within the word for a jail

parts.note: gaol is the British spelling of jail
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, stands for a doctor

explanation.surface: A playful romp ends with a physician being locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To frolic is to skip and leap about playfully, like a young lamb.

clue.text: Immediately heard sound

indicators.note: heard tells us to take the word for at once as it is spoken, then spell it another way

parts.note: straight, as in 'go straight there', means immediately

explanation.surface: Someone instantly picked up a noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise but is the definition as a noun for a narrow sea channel, like Plymouth Sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound is a narrow channel of sea between two land masses, the same thing as a channel or narrows.

clue.text: All the articles one repeated about male person detested

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the article letters go round the letter for male

parts.note: the English articles are an, a and the, taken all together
one of those articles, a, is used a second time

explanation.surface: Every grammatical article, plus a repeat, surrounds a man whom everyone loathes.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accursed or loathed is an object of intense dislike; the word applies to a hated person or thing.

clue.text: In Western state, one is entertained by sportsman, a balloonist

parts.note: Mont is an abbreviation for Montana, a western US state

indicators.note: is entertained by says the letter is welcomed inside the sportsman's word

parts.note: a golfer plays a sport
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Out West, a sportsman hosts a hot-air aviator.
explanation.walkthrough: The Montgolfier brothers flew the first manned hot-air balloon in France in 1783.
explanation.definitionFit: The French brothers who pioneered hot-air flight, so either is a pioneer of aviation.

clue.text: Information having bearing on hereditary element

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Data that relates to an inherited trait.
explanation.definitionFit: A unit of heredity carried on a chromosome is the basic inherited element of biology.

clue.text: Old Italian lady goes round by car, showing advanced age

indicators.note: goes round signals that the Italian woman's title turns back on itself

parts.note: donna is Italian for a lady
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: An elderly Italian woman tours in her small car, revealing her years.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase for 'in the year of our Lord' is used in Britain as slang for old age and its effects.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin dating phrase is British slang for getting on in years, the effects of growing old.

clue.text: It's thoughtless to spoil child being hugged — love it

indicators.note: being hugged says one word is held inside another

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
a lad is a boy, a child
love is zero in tennis, so O

explanation.surface: Spoiling a child by cuddling him is unwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy and tactless, lacking skill or consideration in dealing with things or people.

clue.text: Liberal spread, including what's not on the menu

definitions.text: Liberal spread, including what's not on the menu

indicators.note: including says the letters of one piece are held inside the jumbled word
spread hints at letters scattered about and rearranged

parts.note: a dish that is off is no longer available to order

explanation.surface: A generous buffet includes dishes not normally offered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' gives BILLARE; 'including' holds the dish that is off; read whole, the clue describes the generous list of dishes itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of dishes available at a meal, a liberal spread of food, is a restaurant's menu or card.

clue.text: Soft soap and cloth used for cleaning

definitions.meaning: soft soap is flattery or smooth evasive talk
a small towelling square for washing the face

explanation.definitionFit: The word is British for empty flattery and also for a face cloth, a washcloth.

clue.text: Previous title that's applied to king

parts.note: earl is a noble title
ie, id est, means that is
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A former rank given to a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means before in time, preceding or prior.

clue.text: Device to record opening of orifice

parts.note: to log is to record, as in a ship's log

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A gadget that notes down what goes into a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A device in heraldry or branding is an emblem or symbol, as a company's badge is.

clue.text: Failure to reach target and lag pipes needing treatment

indicators.note: needing treatment suggests the letters must be worked on and rearranged

explanation.surface: A plumber's job falls behind schedule because the pipe lagging needs repair.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippage is a shortfall or falling behind a planned schedule or goal.

clue.text: Very small amount of heroin 23 maiden in final stage of development

clue.text: Shakespearean villain takes in maiden in final stage of development

indicators.note: takes in says one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Iago is the villain of Othello
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare villain seduces a young woman at the last stage of growth.
explanation.definitionFit: An imago is the adult winged insect, the last stage of metamorphosis.

clue.text: This can baffle and strain

definitions.meaning: a puzzling question is something that can bewilder
to strain is to sieve, as through a coarse mesh

explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle question baffles; a coarse sieve for soil strains it, and both senses share the one word.

clue.text: 3 beheaded in part of Spain

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off the word

parts.note: 3-down's answer means a model of perfection, also called a paragon

explanation.surface: A peerless figure loses his head in a Spanish region.
explanation.walkthrough: The 3 points to 3-down; take a synonym of that answer, not the answer itself.
explanation.definitionFit: A former kingdom in north-east Spain, now an autonomous region with Zaragoza as capital.

clue.text: Occasional misconduct is copied

indicators.note: misconduct hints the letters are badly conducted, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing happens now and then when work is plagiarised.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodic means happening at irregular intervals, now and then rather than steadily.

clue.text: Refusal to hear and understand

indicators.note: to hear says the word for refusal is said aloud and spelt as another word

parts.note: no is a refusal

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to listen and grasp the point.
explanation.definitionFit: To understand something is to be aware of it or grasp it.

clue.text: Collection of things written about it potentially real and true

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the little word
potentially says the letters could become something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A body of writing about something that could be genuine and accurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' scrambles the two adjectives to LERATURE; 'about' wraps that round the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Literature is the body of written works, the books of a language or field.
